name: watch.registry
description: Observe registry-key changes. With `until_change: false` (default), returns a subscription_id and emits EVENT frames per change until cancelled. With `until_change: true`, blocks the connection synchronously and returns when the first change fires (one-shot wait — replaces the v2.0 `registry.wait`).

watch_subtree.description: If true, fire on changes anywhere in the key's subtree. Without this, only direct changes to `path` itself trigger.

until_change.description: If true, behave as a synchronous one-shot wait: block the connection until the first change fires (or `timeout_ms` expires), then return with the change payload as the regular sync response — no subscription created, no EVENT frames. If false (default), create a streaming subscription and return its `subscription_id` immediately.

timeout_ms.description: Only meaningful when `until_change: true`. Maximum sync wait in milliseconds. Returns ERR timeout if no change fires within this window. Default 30 seconds. Ignored in subscription mode (subscriptions are open-ended).

x-output-schema.description: Output shape depends on `until_change`. With `until_change: false` (subscription mode), returns `{subscription_id}`. With `until_change: true` (sync one-shot mode), returns the same payload as the EVENT frame: `{path}`.

subscription_id.description: Subscription identifier in `sub:N` form. Present only in subscription mode (`until_change: false`).

path.description: The registry key that changed. Present only in sync one-shot mode (`until_change: true`); echoes the input `path`.

x-event-schema.description: EVENT frames emitted in subscription mode (`until_change: false`). Win32 RegNotifyChangeKeyValue does NOT identify which value changed — the EVENT is a coarse `something in this key changed` signal; consumers re-read the key to see what changed.

path.description: The registry key that changed (echoes the input `path`; useful when multiple watch.registry subscriptions are active on the same connection).

x-implementations.name: reg_notify_change_key_value_loop
x-implementations.description: Win32 `RegNotifyChangeKeyValue` in a loop on a dedicated thread for subscription mode (re-arms after each signal). For `until_change: true`, a single one-shot RegNotifyChangeKeyValue + WaitForMultipleObjects(event, connection_cancel_event, timeout) returns synchronously.

windows-modern.description: RegNotifyChangeKeyValue with REG_NOTIFY_CHANGE_NAME | LAST_SET | ATTRIBUTES | SECURITY classes. Subscription mode re-arms in a loop. Sync mode uses a single arm + WaitForMultipleObjects with the connection-cancel event for clean shutdown.

windows-classic.description: RegNotifyChangeKeyValue available since NT 3.1. Win 9x has limited registry-change support; classic agent on 9x falls back to a polling read loop. Both modes (subscription and until_change) share the polling path on 9x.
